patch.objective: Group statements into a transaction with BEGIN, COMMIT, ROLLBACK and SAVEPOINT, and explain atomicity
secondaryObjectives: Prevent a lost update with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE or a single atomic UPDATE, and compare isolation levels

sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch: a transaction 'bundles multiple steps into a single, all-or-nothing operation'; it is set up with BEGIN and COMMIT, and ROLLBACK cancels 'all our updates so far'; 'The updates made so far by an open transaction are invisible to other transactions until the transaction completes.' The case runs on SQL Server: a session that began a transaction and never committed holds its locks, and every order save waits behind it. Ending the head blocker rolls its work back atomically.

sources.cite: Microsoft Learn, Understand and resolve SQL Server blocking problems (last updated 2026-08-04)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch of the Danish-locale page (English text summarized) on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: 'Identify the main blocking session (head blocker)'; scenario 2, a sleeping SPID with open_transaction_count greater than zero, which a timeout or cancel does not end ('doesn't automatically roll back or commit the transaction'), resolved by the application (IF @@TRANCOUNT > 0 ROLLBACK, SET XACT_ABORT ON) and listed as 'No, but SPID can be killed'; a killed session is marked KILLED/ROLLBACK until the rollback ends; blocked_process_report in Extended Events with the threshold set by sp_configure ('By default, no blocked process reports are produced'). KILL WITH STATUSONLY is not on that page; to verify against the KILL reference.
